name: ID-02
label: Safe R

key_factors: R+13 district partisan lean in a heavily Republican state
Longtime incumbent Mike Simpson with a 10-to-1 fundraising advantage
Democrat Ellie Gilbreath raised only about $107K with no outside support
Prediction markets give Democrats roughly a 5% chance
model.rationale: The baseline of R+15.5 rests on a strong partisan lean, incumbent advantage, and a dominant fundraising gap, with no polls or ratings suggesting movement. I stay essentially at the baseline, shading slightly toward the fundamentals-plus-incumbency picture.
model.watch: A major outside-spending surge for Gilbreath or an unexpected Simpson scandal would be the main ways this moves off Safe R.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Idaho's 2nd District is a solidly Republican seat, with a partisan lean of about R+13, and Mike Simpson has held it for decades. He was renominated and enters the general with a large financial edge, having raised over $1.1 million compared with roughly $107,000 for Democrat Ellie Gilbreath. No independent groups are engaged on either side, and minor-party and independent candidates have raised negligible amounts.

There are no public polls of the race and no expert ratings, so the forecast leans on fundamentals and prediction markets, which put Democratic odds around five percent. The environment favors Republicans this cycle, reinforcing the baseline. Barring an unforeseen development, Simpson is heavily favored to win another term.
